profile.reading: Arcola Tech Park is a commercial land development in eastern Loudoun County, Virginia, part of the St. John Properties portfolio, sited along John Mosby Highway (U.S. Route 50) near the newly built Northstar Boulevard, about two miles from Washington Dulles International Airport. Loudoun County is home to the world's densest cluster of data centers, and St. John Properties markets Arcola Tech Park specifically for that use, describing it in leasing materials as offering by right data center development potential across roughly 1.6 million square feet of buildable space, meaning a data center project there can generally proceed under existing zoning without a separate rezoning case. The broader tract also includes at least one outparcel being marketed for a convenience store rather than a data center. As of the most recent available mapping, the site carries a 2030 target opening date, consistent with a property still in the land planning and pre construction phase rather than an operating facility with a named tenant. No hyperscale or colocation operator has been publicly identified as having leased or purchased the site, and no building, power capacity, or square footage for an actual constructed data center has been published anywhere found in this research. This entry therefore describes a real, actively marketed by right data center development site in the heart of Data Center Alley, not yet a built and operating facility.
profile.research_note: Confirmed as a genuine St. John Properties (sjpi.com) commercial land development in Aldie/Loudoun County VA, marketed explicitly for by-right data center development (up to 1.6M SF). No constructed building, named tenant, or operator confirmed. reading.body:
Arcola Tech Park in Loudoun County is ranked 24th among Virginia facilities by published power capacity, but no megawatt figure is published for this site. The research note indicates this may be an undeveloped pad site within the larger Arcola industrial area rather than an operating data center campus, and no operator or tenant name is documented.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 publish power specifications totaling 1,375 megawatts. The inclusion of Arcola Tech Park in this registry is flagged as uncertain pending clarification of whether an unbuilt or pre-lease site qualifies for tracking.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI infrastructure scaling. If developed, its significance would depend on power capacity, interconnection quality, and available grid headroom in Loudoun County, none of which are currently documented.
